text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which helps both you and your teammates work faster. One key part of clean code is following naming conventions. Use clear and meaningful names for variables and functions so others can see what they do. Another important idea is keeping functions small and simple. Each function should do one job well. This makes code easier to test and fix. Finally, clean code is easier to maintain over time. When code is well organised, you can update it without breaking other parts of the program.
